title: What happens when a fish swallows an eel alive?

lines.text: What happens when a fish swallows an eel alive? It doesn't always stay down.
Japanese scientists fed young eels to a hungry predator fish, and filmed it on X-ray.
Inside the stomach, most eels didn't give up. They swam backwards, up towards the gills.
Thirteen poked their tails out through the gill slit.
Nine wriggled all the way out and swam off. On average it took them fifty-six seconds.
It's the only fish known to escape a stomach. Follow for more interesting cartoons.

experiment.note: FIRST no-Gary Short (george 2026-11-25): animal fact told straight, new underwater set, predator fish with X-ray mode, segmented eel. Hypothesis: a pure animal 'wait, what?' holds as well as Gary stories.

facts.claim: Hasegawa et al. (Current Biology, 2024) filmed juvenile Japanese eels eaten by dark sleeper fish (Odontobutis obscura) with X-ray video
Of 32 eels swallowed, 28 tried to escape by moving back up the gut towards the gills; 13 got their tails out of a gill, 9 escaped completely
Japanese eel is the only fish confirmed to escape a predator's digestive tract after capture (Hasegawa to New Scientist)
